sources.entry: Ergo - Modern IRCv3 server written in Go, combining the features of an ircd, a services framework, and a bouncer. (Source Code) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Ergo is a modern IRCv3 server written in Go that combines an ircd, a services framework, and a bouncer in one program.
summary.what_it_does: Ergo (formerly Oragono) is an IRC server whose stated design goals are simple setup, integrated account management, history storage and bouncer functionality, and strong IRCv3 support. It is described as suitable as an IRCv3 reference implementation. Configuration is a YAML file that can be reloaded at runtime (rehashed) without restarting. Services are built in: users register nicknames and channels, and registered channels remember the owner, topic, and modes. The README points to USERGUIDE.md for end users and MANUAL.md for operators, which hold the detailed feature documentation. The README also notes a public test instance, testnet.ergo.chat, reachable over TLS on port 6697 or plaintext on port 6667.
use_cases: chat server for a community or team
bouncer that keeps IRC history and logins
registering nicknames and channels on IRC
notable: Integrated ircd, services framework, and bouncer in a single server
Bleeding-edge IRCv3 support, suitable as a reference implementation
Built-in account, nickname, and channel registration with history storage
caveats: The README does not include install or build instructions; setup details are in the linked MANUAL.md
